title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Mock Exam #2

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #2
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which part of a plant makes fruits and seeds? (1 mark)
   A. Root
   B. Flower
   C. Stem
   D. Leaf

2. Which of these is a mammal? (1 mark)
   A. Frog
   B. Cow
   C. Crocodile
   D. Tilapia

3. Which of these statements is true? (1 mark)
   A. All small animals are insects
   B. All animals have six legs
   C. All fish have a backbone
   D. All animals can fly

4. Which of these is a good way to care for a farm animal? (1 mark)
   A. Give clean water and shelter
   B. Beat it
   C. Leave it in the rain
   D. Give it dirty water

5. What does the stomach do to food? (1 mark)
   A. Stores faeces
   B. Cuts it into pieces
   C. Takes back water
   D. Churns it and mixes it with juices

6. Which of these is NOT a part of the digestive system? (1 mark)
   A. Rectum
   B. Stomach
   C. Lungs
   D. Gullet

7. When reading a measuring jug, where should your eye be? (1 mark)
   A. Above the jug
   B. Far from the jug
   C. Below the jug
   D. At the same level as the water surface

8. Which unit is used for the volume of milk? (1 mark)
   A. Kilogram
   B. Litre
   C. Gram
   D. Metre

9. What instrument measures the mass of an object? (1 mark)
   A. Measuring jug
   B. Balance
   C. Clock
   D. Thermometer

10. Which are the three states of matter? (1 mark)
   A. Solid, liquid and gas
   B. Big, medium and small
   C. Hot, warm and cold
   D. Hard, soft and rough

11. Which waste is both decomposable and from an animal? (1 mark)
   A. Plastic
   B. Tin
   C. Glass
   D. Dung

12. What are the three Rs? (1 mark)
   A. Reduce, remove and rest
   B. Reduce, reuse and recycle
   C. Recycle, repair and rest
   D. Read, write and run

13. What is the best way to deal with metal scrap in a school? (1 mark)
   A. Throw it in a river
   B. Bury it in the school garden
   C. Sell it to a scrap dealer or reuse it
   D. Burn it

14. What should you do if you find a needle or broken glass in waste? (1 mark)
   A. Put it in your pocket
   B. Play with it
   C. Tell a teacher and do not touch it
   D. Pick it up with bare hands

15. A dripping tap fills a 5 litre bucket in one day. How much water is wasted in 4 days? (1 mark)
   A. 20 litres
   B. 54 litres
   C. 9 litres
   D. 1 litre

16. Why do we wash vegetables in a basin? (1 mark)
   A. It makes them cold
   B. It wastes water
   C. It uses less water and the water can be reused
   D. It makes them heavier

17. Why is saving water good for families? (1 mark)
   A. It reduces the water bill
   B. It stops rain
   C. It causes floods
   D. It makes water heavier

18. Which of these is a reason to conserve water? (1 mark)
   A. To make it more expensive
   B. There will be enough for everyone
   C. To make taps rust
   D. To waste less time

19. Which of these reduces friction? (1 mark)
   A. Gluing parts
   B. Sand on a surface
   C. Rough paint
   D. Ball bearings

20. What effect does friction have on rubbing your hands? (1 mark)
   A. It makes them heavy
   B. It makes them wet
   C. It makes them cold
   D. It makes them warm

21. Which of these makes its own light? (1 mark)
   A. A mirror
   B. A shiny cup
   C. A glow-worm
   D. A white wall

22. How can lights help protect a home? (1 mark)
   A. Security lights help keep thieves away
   B. Lights make walls hot
   C. Lights make doors open
   D. Lights make people sleep

23. When light hits an opaque object, what forms behind it? (1 mark)
   A. A flame
   B. A rainbow
   C. A shadow
   D. Sound

24. Which of these is a natural source of light at night? (1 mark)
   A. A street lamp
   B. A torch
   C. A candle
   D. Stars

25. Which of these is the biggest natural source of light for the Earth? (1 mark)
   A. A star far away
   B. A candle
   C. The sun
   D. The moon

26. Which of these is a safety rule about the sun? (1 mark)
   A. Look at it for a long time
   B. Never look directly at it
   C. Shine a mirror in eyes
   D. Go out at midday without shade

27. How does heat help plants and animals? (1 mark)
   A. It makes them sleepy
   B. It keeps them warm enough to live
   C. It makes them cold
   D. It stops growth

28. Which of these is a use of heat? (1 mark)
   A. Cooking food
   B. Making light only
   C. Hearing sound
   D. Making shadows

29. Which of these is the biggest natural source of heat for the Earth? (1 mark)
   A. An iron
   B. A fire
   C. The sun
   D. A kettle

30. Which of these is a fuel? (1 mark)
   A. Sand
   B. Glass
   C. Clean water
   D. Firewood

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Give three examples of things that use electricity to make heat. (3 marks)

32. Why should we use LED and solar lamps instead of paraffin lamps? Give two reasons. (4 marks)

33. Why is the moon not a source of light? (2 marks)

34. Explain why sorting waste is important for reusing and recycling. (4 marks)

35. Give two examples of decomposable waste and two of non-decomposable waste. (2 marks)

36. Give three safety measures during waste management. (3 marks)

37. List four water-saving habits that pupils can practise at school. (4 marks)

38. Name two roots, two stems and two leaves that people eat. (4 marks)

39. A ball is at rest. Kelvin kicks it, then Mercy stops it with her foot, then she kicks it to the right. Name the effect of the force in each case. (3 marks)

40. Suggest two ways to make toys or ornaments from waste and the materials needed. (4 marks)

41. Explain the importance of conserving water at home and school. (5 marks)

42. Write the function of the rectum and anus. (3 marks)

43. Define matter and give two examples. (2 marks)

44. Explain why a football is described as a container of matter although it looks empty. (3 marks)

45. Give two natural and two artificial sources of light. (2 marks)

46. Name the parts of the digestive system in the order food passes through them. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #2 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Flower
   Flowers make fruits that contain seeds.

2. B — Cow
   A cow has hair and feeds its calf on milk.

3. C — All fish have a backbone
   Fish are vertebrates. Small animals may be spiders, worms or others.

4. A — Give clean water and shelter
   Farm animals need water, food, shelter and care.

5. D — Churns it and mixes it with juices
   The stomach churns food into a thick soup with digestive juices.

6. C — Lungs
   Lungs are for breathing.

7. D — At the same level as the water surface
   This gives an accurate reading.

8. B — Litre
   Liquid volume is measured in millilitres and litres.

9. B — Balance
   A balance is used to measure mass.

10. A — Solid, liquid and gas
   Matter exists as solids, liquids and gases.

11. D — Dung
   Animal dung rots and can be used as manure.

12. B — Reduce, reuse and recycle
   Reduce, reuse and recycle are ways of managing waste.

13. C — Sell it to a scrap dealer or reuse it
   Metal can be recycled.

14. C — Tell a teacher and do not touch it
   Sharp objects should be handled by adults using tools.

15. A — 20 litres
   5 x 4 = 20 litres.

16. C — It uses less water and the water can be reused
   A basin limits water use and allows reuse.

17. A — It reduces the water bill
   Less water used means less money paid.

18. B — There will be enough for everyone
   Conserving leaves water for others.

19. D — Ball bearings
   Ball bearings roll and reduce friction.

20. D — It makes them warm
   Friction produces heat.

21. C — A glow-worm
   Glow-worms produce their own light.

22. A — Security lights help keep thieves away
   Thieves avoid places where they can be seen.

23. C — A shadow
   Blocked light makes a shadow.

24. D — Stars
   Stars give out their own light.

25. C — The sun
   The sun lights the Earth in the daytime.

26. B — Never look directly at it
   The sun can harm eyes.

27. B — It keeps them warm enough to live
   Life needs suitable warmth.

28. A — Cooking food
   Heat cooks food.

29. C — The sun
   The sun heats the Earth.

30. D — Firewood
   Fuels burn to give heat.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: Electric kettle, iron, cooker, heater, hair dryer, toaster.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: They are safer with less fire risk and less smoke. Solar lamps use free energy and are cheaper to use.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each reason.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: It does not make its own light. It reflects light from the sun.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for no light of its own and 1 mark for reflecting sunlight.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: Sorting separates plastics, metals, glass, paper and food waste so each can be recycled, reused or composted without contaminating the others.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for sorting, 1 mark for recycling, 1 mark for composting, 1 mark for clear link.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: Decomposable: vegetable peelings, dung, leaves. Non-decomposable: plastic, tin, glass.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: Wear gloves and closed shoes, use a rake or shovel, do not touch sharp objects, wash hands afterwards, do not burn waste.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

37. (4 marks)
   Answer: Close taps, report leaks, use a bucket for watering the garden, water plants in the morning or evening, use a cup to drink.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

38. (4 marks)
   Answer: Roots: carrot, cassava, sweet potato. Stems: sugarcane. Leaves: cabbage, sukuma wiki, spinach (any two of each, with correct grouping).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair and 1 mark for correct grouping overall.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: Kelvin starts motion, Mercy stops motion, Mercy's second kick changes direction.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct effect.

40. (4 marks)
   Answer: A toy car from a box and bottle tops. Beads from rolled paper. A flower vase from a tin.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each toy and 1 mark for each list of materials.

41. (5 marks)
   Answer: There is enough water for all, we save money, animals and crops get water, it reduces work of fetching water and protects sources.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason up to 5.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: The rectum stores faeces for a short time and the anus is the opening through which faeces leave the body.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for rectum, 1 mark for anus, 1 mark for describing waste leaving.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: Matter is anything that has mass and takes up space. Examples: water, stone, air.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 mark for two examples.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is full of air. Air is a gas, so it has mass and takes up space. It keeps the ball in shape.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for air inside, 1 mark for air being matter, 1 mark for it filling the ball.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: Natural: sun, stars, lightning, firefly. Artificial: bulb, torch, candle, lantern, solar lamp.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two correct natural and 1 mark for two correct artificial.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: Mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, rectum, anus.
   Working / marking points: Award 2 marks for the correct order. 1 mark if at most two parts are out of order.
